title: The horse that read the room

probes.question: What was Clever Hans actually responding to?
options: Involuntary cues in his trainer's body language
A bell rung by a hidden helper

probes.question: True or false: when Hans could not see the questioner, he still answered most questions correctly.

image.alt: Black-and-white 1907 photograph of the horse Clever Hans standing in a brick courtyard while a group of men in hats look on.
image.credit: unbekannt, Urheberrecht lag bei Karl Krall / Wikimedia Commons

panels.text: Clever Hans was a horse that appeared to perform arithmetic and other intellectual tasks during exhibitions in Germany in the early 20th century.
His owner, Wilhelm von Osten, asked the questions. Hans answered by tapping his hoof.
In 1907, psychologist Oskar Pfungst demonstrated that the horse was not actually performing these mental tasks, but was watching the reactions of his trainer.
When Hans could see the questioner, he got 89 percent (50 out of 56) of the answers correct. When he could not, he got six percent (2 out of 35).
